incumbent_league_coverage_gap.finding: src/model_prediction/rebuild/providers/soccer_espn.py's ESPN_SOCCER_LEAGUES dict hardcodes only 6 league codes (eng.1/esp.1/ger.1/ita.1/fra.1/usa.1). The incumbent's own src/model_prediction/data_sources/espn.py LEAGUE_PATHS dict supports all of the incumbent's 19 configured leagues (including UCL, BRASILEIRAO, ARGENTINA, SUDAMERICANA, FRIENDLIES, etc via distinct ESPN codes like uefa.champions/bra.1/arg.1/conmebol.sudamericana/fifa.friendly), but that dict is not reused by the rebuild's soccer_espn.py provider. Passing an unsupported code (e.g. --espn-league uefa.champions) to rebuild-data returns UNAVAILABLE ('unsupported ESPN soccer league') rather than reaching ESPN, confirmed by code inspection of ESPNSoccerProvider._league(). 13 of the incumbent's 19 configured leagues (all of South America, UCL, and both friendly buckets) are currently unreachable through the rebuild's soccer data foundation. This is a real, scoped gap worth closing in a future pass (extend ESPN_SOCCER_LEAGUES to mirror data_sources/espn.py's LEAGUE_PATHS) -- not fixed in this pass per the 'no model-fitting code, pure data-foundation groundwork' scope.

team_identity_and_collision_check.finding: Zero collisions found in the collected sample (128 distinct team_ids, 128 distinct team_id/name pairs, no id mapping to >1 name and no name mapping to >1 id). This is a structurally different identity scheme from the incumbent's known bug (docs DEBUG.md 2026-07-31: soccer_forward.py's _team_matches_title fuzzy word-matching collided 'Manchester United' with 'Manchester City' via generic-word stripping) -- that bug lives entirely in the incumbent's Polymarket market-title-matching layer (name-string fuzzy matching against market titles), which the rebuild has not built yet (match_markets stage is STAGE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED for soccer, see sport_adapter.py/_BasicEloAdapter routing). The rebuild's own normalized match data keys team identity by ESPN's numeric team_id, which cannot reproduce that specific string-collision bug class. However, this does NOT mean the risk is retired project-wide: once a real rebuild match_markets stage is eventually built (matching normalized matches to Polymarket contract titles by name), the same class of fuzzy-name-collision risk reappears at that seam and would need its own explicit guard -- this backfill only confirms the rebuild's *storage/identity* layer is collision-free today, not that the eventual market-matching layer will be.

pit_and_provenance_checks.capture_time_only_caveat: Every normalized row carries availability_basis='capture_time_only' -- observed_at_utc/available_at_utc reflect when THIS backfill run captured the row (2026-08-11), not the real historical game date (event_start_utc). This matches the project-wide pattern already documented for mlb_v3 ('no claim that capture-time historical snapshots are retrospective PIT data', docs/rebuild/MLB_V3_DATA.md) and wnba/nfl/tennis foundations. Consequence: eligible_matches_as_of()/prior_team_matches_as_of() (pit.py), which gate on observed_at_utc<=decision_time, would treat this entire backfilled corpus as unavailable for any decision_time before the capture run -- i.e. this data is NOT yet walk-forward-simulation-safe under the live-serving PIT contract. A future model-fitting phase must explicitly decide whether to (a) train on event_start_utc as the real-world PIT boundary for completed/immutable final scores (score doesn't change after completed=True, so this is defensible for training even though it isn't 'proof of live availability'), or (b) commit to ongoing day-by-day prospective collection to build genuine per-day capture provenance. Neither is decided anywhere in this repo -- rebuild-model reports NOT_IMPLEMENTED for every sport, so there is no existing precedent to follow.
